This report is requesting approval to draft the new Saskatoon Transit by law, along with two minor corresponding by law amendments. This works stems from Council's previous direction to enhance safety on Saskatoon Transit, including the approval of the transit policing program in the

2020-27 budget. In collaboration with the Saskatoon Police Service, and with input from a malagomated transit union local 615, administration is developed by law framework that formalizes safety expectations and provides officers with clear practical tools to address unsafe or disruptive behavior.

The proposed by law includes four key enforcement mechanisms. First, it grants officers the authority to remove individuals from transit property or prohibit entry when someone is engaging in unacceptable behavior.
This includes violations of laws or by laws or any behavior that threatens the health, safety, comfort or security of others.
Second, it establishes the ability to issue temporary or longer-term bans from transit services. The doom by law will allow officers to issue temporary, non-appealable bans of up to 24 hours.

Longer-term bans or restrictions may be imposed by Saskatoon Transit were considered appropriate, such as in response to incidences of more serious inappropriate behavior or incidents of repeated misbehavior.

The by-law will give persons the right to appeal longer-term bans to the Saskatoon appeal board. Third, the by-law creates transit-specific offenses such as distracting an operator or placing feet on seats with a proposed fine of $50.
This complements existing enforcement tools under other city by-laws and provincial or federal legislation.
Fourthly, it is recommended that the new by-law include provisions that require persons to pay the required fair amount at the time of boarding and to provide proof of payment upon request.
This would enable officers to remove or take a passengers who fail to pay the required fair or who fail to provide proof of payment upon request.
The report also recommends incorporating the existing transit fairs by-law into this new by-law, creating one comprehensive regulatory framework for Saskatoon Transit.

Two minor amendments are also proposed expanding the public-spitting urination and defecation prohibition by-law to include transit property and updating the Saskatoon appeal board by-law, so all transit-related appeals follow a consistent process.
Finally, this by-law will be supported by the upcoming transit code education campaign, launching later this year to help set clear expectations for riders.
If approved, the city solicitor will prepare the by-laws for council's consideration at the July Council meeting with a planned effective date of September 1, 2026.
